readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: Discovering the Rehearsal of Sukkot
readings.subtitle: The leadership examines the Torah and uncovers the mandated appointed time to dwell in booths.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 8:13] And on the second day the heads of the fathers’ houses of all the people, with the priests and Lěvites, were gathered to Ezra the scribe, in order to study the words of the Torah. [14] And they found written in the Torah, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded by Mosheh, that the children of Yisra’ěl should dwell in booths in the festival of the seventh new moon, [15] and that they should announce and proclaim in all their cities and in Yerushalayim, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and bring olive branches, branches of oil trees, and myrtle branches, and palm branches, and branches of leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written.”

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: The Physical Execution of the Command
readings.subtitle: The assembly physically aligns with the ancient instruction, initiating unprecedented rejoicing and daily Torah study.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 8:16] So the people went out and brought them and made themselves booths, each one on the roof of his house, and in their courtyards and in the courtyards of the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and in the open space of the Water Gate and in the open space of the Gate of Ephrayim. [17] And the entire assembly of those who had come back from the captivity made booths and sat under the booths, for since the days of Yěshua son of Nun until that day the children of Yisra’ěl had not done so. And there was very great rejoicing. [18] And day by day, from the first day until the last day, he read from the Book of the Torah of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And they performed the festival seven days. And on the eighth day there was an assembly, according to the right-ruling.

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: Structural Separation and Confession
readings.subtitle: The seed of Yisra’ěl permanently separates from foreign influence to publicly confess systemic failures and bless the Name.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 9:1] And on the twenty-fourth day of this new moon the children of Yisra’ěl were assembled with fasting, and in sackcloth, and with earth on them. [2] And the descendants of Yisra’ěl separated themselves from all foreigners, and stood and confessed their sins, and the crookednesses of their fathers, [3] and they stood up in their place and read from the Book of the Torah of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn> a fourth part of the day, and a fourth part they were confessing and worshipping <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: The Lěvitical Call to Worship
readings.subtitle: The appointed Lěvites step forward to lead the assembly in exalting the exclusive Name of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 9:4] Then Yěshua and Bani, Qaḏmi’ěl, Sheḇanyah, Bunni, Shěrěḇyah, Bani, Kenani stood on the stairs of the Lěvites and cried out with a loud voice to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>. [5] Then the Lěvites, Yěshua and Qaḏmi’ěl, Bani, Ḥashaḇneyah, Shěrěḇyah, Hoḏiyah, Sheḇanyah, Pethaḥyah, said, “Rise, bless <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> forever and ever! And let them bless <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> esteemed Name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise!

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: The Singular Creator and the Abrahamic Guarantee
readings.subtitle: Acknowledging YeHoVaH as the strict, singular architect of the cosmos and the guarantor of the territorial covenant with Aḇraham.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 9:6] “<dn>You</dn> are <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> alone. <dn>You</dn> have made <dn>את</dn> the heavens, the heavens of the heavens, with all their host, <dn>את</dn> the earth and all that are on it, <dn>את</dn> the seas and all that are in them, and <dn>You</dn> give life to them all. And the host of the heavens are bowing themselves to <dn>You</dn>. [7] “<dn>You</dn> are <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> who chose Aḇram, and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldees, and gave him the name of Aḇraham, [8] and found <dn>את</dn> his heart trustworthy before <dn>You</dn>, and made a covenant with him to give <dn>את</dn> the land of the Kena‛anites, the Ḥittites, the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Yeḇusites, and the Girgashites – to give it to his seed. And <dn>You</dn> have established <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> words, for <dn>You</dn> are righteous,

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: Intervention and the Impartation of Truth
readings.subtitle: Recounting the decisive extraction from the crucible of Mitsrayim and the transmission of straight right-rulings and the Sabbath at Sinai.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 9:9] and saw <dn>את</dn> the affliction of our fathers in Mitsrayim, and heard <dn>את</dn> their cry by the Sea of Reeds, [10] and gave signs and wonders against Pharaoh, and against all his servants, and against all the people of his land. For <dn>You</dn> knew that they acted proudly against them. And <dn>You</dn> made a Name for <dn>Yourself</dn>, as it is this day. [11] “And <dn>You</dn> split the sea before them, and they passed over into the midst of the sea on the dry land. And <dn>את</dn> their pursuers <dn>You</dn> threw into the deep as a stone into the mighty waters. [12] “And <dn>You</dn> led them by day with a cloudy column, and by night with a column of fire, to give them light in the way they were to go. [13] “And <dn>You</dn> came down on Mount Sinai, and spoke with them from the heavens, and gave them straight right-rulings and Torot of truth, good laws and commands. [14] “And <dn>You</dn> made known to them <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Sabbath, and <dn>You</dn> commanded them commands and laws and Torot, by the hand of Mosheh <dn>Your</dn> servant. [15] “And <dn>You</dn> gave them bread from the heavens for their hunger, and brought them water out of the rock for their thirst, and said to them to go in to possess <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>You</dn> had sworn to give them.

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: Wilderness Friction and Divine Sustenance
readings.subtitle: Despite severe rebellion and a desire to return to bondage, the Creator maintains His loving-commitment, providing His Spirit, manna, and water.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 9:16] “But they and our fathers acted proudly, and hardened their necks, and did not obey <dn>Your</dn> commands. [17] “And they refused to obey, and they remembered not <dn>Your</dn> wonders that <dn>You</dn> did among them, and hardened their necks, and in their rebellion they appointed a leader to return to their bondage. But <dn>You</dn> are a forgiving <dn>Eloah</dn>, showing favour, and compassionate, patient, and of great loving-commitment, and did not forsake them. [18] “Even when they made a moulded calf for themselves, and said, ‘This is your mighty one that brought you up out of Mitsrayim,’ and worked great blasphemies, [19] yet <dn>You</dn>, in <dn>Your</dn> great compassion did not forsake them in the wilderness. The column of the cloud did not turn away from them by day to lead them on the way, nor the column of fire by night to give them light in the way they were to go. [20] “<dn>You</dn> also gave <dn>Your</dn> good Spirit to instruct them, and did not withhold <dn>Your</dn> manna from their mouth, and gave them water for their thirst. [21] “And for forty years <dn>You</dn> sustained them in the wilderness – they lacked not. Their garments did not wear out and their feet did not swell.

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: The Transfer of Territorial Authority
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH humbles the rebellious nations of Kena‛an, granting Yisra’ěl possession of a rich, surplus-generating land.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 9:22] “And <dn>You</dn> gave them reigns and peoples, and apportioned them their lot. So they took possession of <dn>את</dn> the land of Siḥon, and <dn>את</dn> the land of the sovereign of Ḥeshbon, and <dn>את</dn> the land of Oḡ sovereign of Bashan. [23] “And <dn>You</dn> increased their children as the stars of the heavens, and brought them into the land which <dn>You</dn> had said to their fathers to go in and possess. [24] “So the sons went in and possessed the land, and <dn>You</dn> humbled before them <dn>את</dn> the people of the land, the Kena‛anites, and gave them into their hands, with <dn>את</dn> their sovereigns and <dn>את</dn> the people of the land, to do with them as they desired. [25] “And they captured walled cities and a rich land, and possessed houses filled with all good, cisterns already dug, vineyards, and olive-trees, and fruit trees, in plenty. So they ate and were satisfied and grew fat, and delighted themselves in <dn>Your</dn> great goodness.

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: The Cycle of Lawlessness and Compassionate Rescue
readings.subtitle: A devastating historical pattern of casting the Torah aside, enduring retributive distress, and crying out for unmerited deliverance.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 9:26] “But they became disobedient and rebelled against <dn>You</dn>, and cast <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> Torah behind their backs. And they kill <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> prophets who had warned them, to bring them back to <dn>Yourself</dn>. And they worked great blasphemies. [27] “Therefore <dn>You</dn> gave them into the hand of their enemies, who distressed them. And in the time of their distress, when they cried to <dn>You</dn>, <dn>You</dn> heard from the heavens. And according to <dn>Your</dn> great compassion <dn>You</dn> gave them saviours who saved them from the hand of their enemies. [28] “But after they had rest, they turned back to do evil before <dn>You</dn>. Then <dn>You</dn> left them in the hand of their enemies, so that they ruled over them. But when they turned back and cried out to <dn>You</dn>, <dn>You</dn> heard from the heavens, and delivered them according to <dn>Your</dn> compassion, many times, [29] and warned them, to bring them back to <dn>Your</dn> Torah. But they acted proudly, and did not obey <dn>Your</dn> commands, and sinned against <dn>Your</dn> right-rulings, <dq>which if a man does, he shall live by them.</dq> And they gave the rebellious shoulder and hardened their necks, and would not hear. [30] “And <dn>You</dn> had patience with them for many years, and did warn them by <dn>Your</dn> Spirit, by the hand of <dn>Your</dn> prophets, yet they would not give ear. Therefore <dn>You</dn> gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands. [31] “But in <dn>Your</dn> great compassion <dn>You</dn> did not make an end of them nor forsake them, for <dn>You</dn> are an <dn>Ěl</dn> of favour and compassion.

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: Acknowledging Absolute Divine Justice
readings.subtitle: The assembly confesses their historical guilt, recognizing that YeHoVaH's judgments have been perfectly righteous and true.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 9:32] “And now, our <dn>Elohim</dn>, the great, the mighty, and awesome <dn>Ěl</dn>, guarding the covenant and the loving-commitment, let not all the trouble that has come upon us, our sovereigns and our heads, our priests and our prophets, our fathers and on all <dn>Your</dn> people, from the days of the sovereigns of Ashshur until this day, seem little before <dn>You</dn>. [33] “And in all that has come upon us <dn>You</dn> are righteous, for <dn>You</dn> have done truth, but we have done wrong. [34] “And our sovereigns, our rulers, our priests, and our fathers, have not done <dn>Your</dn> Torah, nor heeded <dn>Your</dn> commands and <dn>Your</dn> witnesses, with which <dn>You</dn> witnessed against them. [35] “For they have not served <dn>You</dn> in their reign, or in <dn>Your</dn> great goodness that <dn>You</dn> gave them, or in the large and rich land which <dn>You</dn> set before them – neither turned back from their evil deeds.

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: Slaves in the Land of Promise
readings.subtitle: Facing the physical consequences of their systemic debt, the leadership drafts a firm, trustworthy pledge of obedience.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 9:36] “See, we are servants today! And the land that <dn>You</dn> gave to our fathers, to eat <dn>את</dn> its fruit and <dn>את</dn> the good of it, see, we are servants in it! [37] “And its rich yield goes to the sovereigns <dn>You</dn> have set over us, because of our sins. And they rule over our bodies and our livestock at their pleasure, and we are in great distress. [38] “And because of all this, we are making a trustworthy pledge, and write it. And our rulers, our Lěvites, our priests set their seal on it.”

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: The Signatories of the Restored Covenant
readings.subtitle: The official registry of the governors, priests, and leaders who set their seal to the renewed agreement.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 10:1] And those who set their seal were: Neḥemyah the governor, son of Ḥaḵalyah, and Tsiḏqiyah, [2] Serayah, Azaryah, Yirmeyah, [3] Pashḥur, Amaryah, Malkiyah, [4] Ḥattush, Sheḇanyah, Malluḵ, [5] Ḥarim, Merěmoth, Oḇaḏyah, [6] Dani’ěl, Ginnethon, Baruḵ, [7] Meshullam, Aḇiyah, Miyamin, [8] Ma‛azyah, Bilgai, and Shemayah. These were the priests. [9] And the Lěvites: both Yěshua son of Atsanyah, Binnui of the sons of Ḥěnaḏaḏ, Qaḏmi’ěl. [10] And their brothers: Sheḇanyah, Hoḏiyah, Qelita, Pelayah, Ḥanan, [11] Miḵa, Reḥoḇ, Ḥashaḇyah, [12] Zakkur, Shěrěḇyah, Sheḇanyah, [13] Hoḏiyah, Bani, and Beninu. [14] The leaders of the people: Parosh, Paḥath-Mo’aḇ, Ěylam, Zattu, Bani, [15] Bunni, Azgaḏ, Běḇai, [16] Aḏoniyah, Biḡvai, Aḏin, [17] Atěr, Ḥizqiyah, Azzur, [18] Hoḏiyah, Ḥashum, Bětsai, [19] Ḥariph, Anathoth, Něḇai, [20] Maḡpi‛ash, Meshullam, Ḥězir, [21] Meshěyzaḇ’ěl, Tsaḏoq, Yaddua, [22] Pelatyah, Ḥanan, Anayah, [23] Hoshěa, Ḥananyah, Ḥashshuḇ, [24] Halloḥěsh, Pilḥa, Shoḇěq, [25] Reḥum, Ḥashaḇnah, Ma‛asěyah, [26] Aḥiyah, Ḥanan, Anan, [27] Malluḵ, Ḥarim, Ba‛anah.

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: The Corporate Oath of the Remnant
readings.subtitle: The broader assembly binds themselves under oath to meticulously guard and execute all the commands of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 10:28] And the rest of the people, the priests, the Lěvites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and all those who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands unto the Torah of <dn>Elohim</dn>, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, all who had knowledge and understanding, [29] were strengthening their brothers, their nobles, and were entering into a curse and into an oath to walk in the Torah of <dn>Elohim</dn>, which was given by Mosheh the servant of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and to guard and do <dn>את</dn> all the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our Master, and <dn>His</dn> right-rulings and <dn>His</dn> laws,

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: Economic and Marital Separation
readings.subtitle: Establishing strict boundaries against foreign intermarriage and halting all commercial activity on the Sabbath.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 10:30] and that we would not give our daughters as wives to the peoples of the land, nor take <dn>את</dn> their daughters for our sons, [31] and that if the peoples of the land bring wares or any grain to sell on the Sabbath day, we would not buy it from them on the Sabbath, or on a set-apart day, and we would forego the seventh year and the interest of every hand.

readings.section: The Restoration of the Covenant Architecture
readings.title: Funding the Architecture of Worship
readings.subtitle: The people impose tithes and first-fruit offerings upon themselves to ensure the continuous operation of the House of Elohim.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 10:32] And we imposed commands on ourselves, to give from ourselves yearly one-third of a sheqel for the service of the House of our <dn>Elohim</dn>: [33] for the showbread, and for the continual grain offering, and for the continual ascending offering of the Sabbaths, of the New moons, for the appointed times, and for the set-apart offerings, and for the sin offerings to make atonement for Yisra’ěl, and all the work of the House of our <dn>Elohim</dn>. [34] And we cast lots among the priests, and the Lěvites, and the people, for bringing the wood offering into the House of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, according to our fathers’ houses, at the appointed times year by year, to burn on the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> as it is written in the Torah, [35] and to bring <dn>את</dn> the first-fruits of our soil and <dn>את</dn> the first-fruits of all fruit of all trees, year by year, to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [36] also to bring <dn>את</dn> the first-born of our sons and our livestock, as it is written in the Torah, and <dn>את</dn> the firstlings of our herds and our flocks, to the House of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to the priests attending in the House of our <dn>Elohim</dn>. [37] And that we should bring <dn>את</dn> the first-fruits of our dough, and our contributions, and the fruit from all kinds of trees, of new wine and of oil, to the priests, to the storerooms of the House of our <dn>Elohim</dn>; and <dn>את</dn> the tithes of our land to the Lěvites, for the Lěvites should receive the tithes in all our rural towns. [38] And the priest, son of Aharon, shall be with the Lěvites when the Lěvites receive tithes, and the Lěvites bring up <dn>את</dn> a tenth of the tithes to the House of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to the rooms of the storehouse. [39] For the children of Yisra’ěl and the children of Lěvi bring <dn>את</dn> the offering of the grain, of the new wine and the oil, to the storerooms where the vessels of the set-apart place are, where the priests who attend and the gatekeepers and the singers are, and we should not neglect <dn>את</dn> the House of our <dn>Elohim</dn>.
